doe-osti-3007762-investigating-solutions:
Final technical report for DOE grant DE-SC0025242, by Keisuke Harigaya of the University of Chicago, covers work from May 2024 to March 2025 on the strong CP problem. Theory expects strong CP violation a billion billion times larger than observation allows, and the mismatch has driven decades of model building.

Three studies anchor the report. A rotating axion field that changes behaviour near recombination can ease the Hubble tension while also generating the cosmic baryon asymmetry. Domain walls bounded by cosmic strings would sing in gravitational waves across many detector bands. A third solution embeds QCD colour into a larger grand-colour group with massless quarks, predicting vector-like quarks near the TeV scale.
